title: H^2 vanishing on affine curves reduces to smooth affine connected curves
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Assume that for every connected curve $C'$ over $k$ [def-sc-curves] (nonempty, connected, of dimension one) which is smooth over $k$ and an affine scheme, and for every torsion abelian sheaf $F'$ on $C'_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], one has $H^2(C'_{\Et},F')=0$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Then for every affine curve $C$ over $k$ [def-sc-curves] (an affine scheme, separated and of finite type over $k$, of dimension at most one; possibly empty, disconnected, singular or with zero-dimensional components) and every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $C_{\Et}$, one has $H^2(C_{\Et},F)=0$.
